overview.title: Trace a value across a function boundary

nodes.label: Caller supplies a value
code: // The integer is converted to uint64_t.

overview.explanation: Arrows show value and execution flow. This is a source-level trace, not a claim about a particular CPU instruction sequence.

focus.title: Separate the interface from the expression
explain: std::uint64_t is an unsigned integer type with exactly 64 value bits on platforms that provide it. The parameter x is a value copy.
Parentheses compute x+5 first; multiplication then produces the result. return passes that value to the caller.
The closing brace ends the function body.
focus.what: The function maps one unsigned input value to one unsigned output value.
focus.where: Its declaration and body are visible to the compiler before main.
focus.why: A named function provides one place to inspect and change this arithmetic rule.
focus.invariant: For the fixture 7, the intermediate is 12 and the result is 48. Unsigned arithmetic wraps modulo 2^64 if its range is exceeded.
focus.risk: Assuming these are unbounded mathematical integers gives wrong results for large inputs. The source alone does not promise one particular machine instruction sequence.

focus.title: Observe rather than assume
explain: main begins the program’s entry-point body.
The nested call completes before its result is inserted into cout. The string adds a newline.
The closing brace ends main; falling off the end is equivalent to returning zero.
focus.what: Output exposes a result that can be checked in a test.
focus.where: This is the runtime caller of transform.
focus.why: A tiny input and exact output help debug arithmetic before inspecting generated instructions.
focus.invariant: For this fixture the output is 48 followed by a newline.
focus.risk: A different integer width or changed operator order may change results; keep tests near the rule.
